subject: Enforcing boxplot widths when overlaying on to geom point

messages.author: a79bb39e464c0da0
messages.subject: Enforcing boxplot widths when overlaying on to geom point
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying overlay a boxplot on a scatter plot. Is there any way to set an enforced width to make the boxplot more readable?

I have two continuous axes, but the data are quantized, such that there are alot of overlapping points. I'd like to show the range of each quantized step, as well as the overall regression.

Actual use: I have mean bill lengths of several hummingbirds species, and i want to plot them against mean corolla lengths of flower species. I want to show the distribution corollas used by each bird, as well as the overall relationship across species. 

See here for the Rmarkdown(sorry, looks like google groups don't read markdown?): https://github.com/bw4sz/Maquipicuna/blob/master/Markdown/BoxplotOverlay.md

Thanks!
Ben Weinstein

messages.subject: Re: Enforcing boxplot widths when overlaying on to geom point
parts:
Borrowing from an idea of Winston Chang's posted a couple of years ago
in this group, here is a toy example that should illustrate what you
want:

DF <- data.frame(x = rep(c(1, 3, 4, 6, 10), each = 50),
y = sample(2:60, 250, replace = TRUE))

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(DF, aes(x = x, y = y, color = factor(x))) +
geom_boxplot(aes(group = x)) +
geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.04)) +
geom_smooth(aes(group = 1))

The idea is that you group the unique x-values for the boxplots, which
should have a 1-1 correspondence with the variable mapped to color.
Notice the use of factor(x) for color to yield a discrete set for the
legend but otherwise x is numeric. You also need group = 1 for the
smooth since color is mapped discretely to x in the base layer.

Since you mentioned you have overlapping points in the data, there's a
chance that jittering points would be sufficient if you contain the
jitter width (and/or height). If you can jitter the points well, the
box plot is really unnecessary and is actually a bit of a distraction
if the point is to look at the relationship between bill length and
corolla length.

Dennis
